answers.text:
The diagram show how the rain water is collect and clean in a public building for use it again.

Firstly, the rain fall on the roof of the building. The gutters and the pipes take this water and it go to a leaf screen. This screen clean the leaf and the grit from the water.

Secondly, the water go to a big tank under the ground and it stay there. When the tank is full the water go out to the drain.

Thirdly, a pump take the water up to the treatment. There is a sand filter and it take the small particle from the water. After this there is a ultraviolet unit and it kill the bacteria, so the water is clean now.

Finally the water go to another tank in the top of the building. From this tank the people use the water for the toilet and for the plants. This system is very good for save the water and the money of the building.

why_this_band.task_response: Most of the nine stages are given in the right order, but the process as a whole (ending in two outlets, being unmanned) is never summarised anywhere. The final sentence adds information that is not in the diagram: money and saving.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: The Firstly / Secondly / Thirdly / Finally pattern is present and the order is correct, so the process can be followed. But the links between stages never go beyond these four words.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: The verbs take and go carry every stage; process-specific words such as collect, filter, store are not reused. For save the water is a form error.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: The passive is attempted then abandoned (is collect and clean), and agreement errors appear in every paragraph: it go, it kill, a ultraviolet unit. Structures amount to simple sentences only.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Form the passive correctly (is collected, is filtered), and drop the final sentence, replacing it with an overview stating where the process begins and ends.

answers.text:
The diagram shows how rainwater is collected and cleaned so that it can be used inside a public building.

Overall, there are nine stages in this process, and it is a linear process which starts with the rain on the roof and finishes with two different uses of the water. The water is also cleaned two times before it is used.

First of all, the rain falls on the roof of the building and the gutters and the pipes collect it. After that, the water arrives to a leaf screen, where the leaves and the grit are taken away. Then the water is stored in a tank which is under the ground. If there is too much water, the extra water goes to the drain.

In the next stage, a pump takes the water up from the tank to the treatment unit. The water goes through a sand filter first, which cleans the small particles, and after that an ultraviolet unit kills the bacteria in the water.

Finally, the clean water is kept in a header tank. From this tank the water is distributed for two purposes: the toilets and watering the plants. The water is not used for drinking.

why_this_band.task_response: All stages are given in the right order and with the right names; the overflow pipe and the two separate points of use are not skipped. There is an overview, but it settles for counting the number of stages rather than saying how the process works.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: The chain First of all, After that, In the next stage, Finally is correct and trackable, but predictably mechanical. Paragraphs are split by the collection, storage and treatment stages.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Suitable words such as collect, store, distribute, treatment unit are present. Arrives to and cleans the small particles are wrong as collocations.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: The passive is used correctly throughout, and relative clauses work. The remaining errors are at preposition and unnecessary article level (arrives to a leaf screen, the leaves and the grit are taken away), few in number and do not block meaning.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Move the overview away from counting stages and towards stating the process's key feature: it is linear, uses a single machine and ends in two different outlets.

answers.text:
The diagram illustrates the stages by which rainwater is captured from the roof of a public building, treated, and then put back to use inside it.

Overall, the process is linear and, apart from a single pump, appears to run without human intervention: it begins with rain falling on the roof and ends at two separate points of use, with an overflow returning any surplus to the drain. Cleaning takes place in two distinct phases, one mechanical and one designed to remove bacteria.

At the start, rain that lands on the roof is channelled into gutters and pipes and directed towards a leaf screen, where leaves and grit are strained out before the water travels any further. It is then stored in an underground tank; once this tank is full, the excess simply runs off into the drain.

When the water is needed, a pump lifts it out of the tank and into the treatment unit. Here it first passes through a sand filter, which catches the fine particles that the screen could not, and it is then exposed to ultraviolet light in order to destroy any remaining bacteria.

Finally, the treated water is held in a header tank, from which it is distributed to its two uses: flushing the toilets and watering plants. At no stage is it made fit for drinking.

why_this_band.task_response: The overview talks about the shape of the process: linear, almost unmanned, two outlets and a two-stage treatment. All stages are covered, including the overflow pipe and the fact that it is not drinking water.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: Stages are grouped as collection, storage, treatment and distribution; transitions such as At the start, When the water is needed, Finally are used as much as needed. Reference words (it, this tank) are clear.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Items such as captured, channelled, strained out, surplus, exposed to, fit for drinking are natural and exactly in place. The mechanical / designed to remove bacteria distinction sums up the treatment.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: The passive, time clauses and a purpose structure (in order to) rotate flexibly. Errors are rare; the inverted closing built with At no stage is controlled.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Give the number of stages as a figure once, and point out earlier that the pump is the process's only mechanical part.
